**Problem Statement:** In aerospace design, the lift force generated by airflow over an aircraft wing profile can be modeled conceptually using the fluid circulation vector ($\vec{\Gamma}$) and the free-stream air velocity vector ($\vec{v}$). According to the Kutta-Joukowski theorem, the lift force vector per unit span ($\vec{F}_L$) is proportional to their cross product: $\vec{F}_L = \rho (\vec{v} \times \vec{\Gamma})$, where $\rho$ is the air density.

Let the air velocity flowing horizontally along the wing chord be $\vec{v} = \langle 150, 0, 0 \rangle\text{ m/s}$ and the circulation bound around the airfoil be $\vec{\Gamma} = \langle 0, 4, 0 \rangle\text{ m}^2/\text{s}$. If the air density at altitude is $\rho = 1.2\text{ kg/m}^3$, find the resulting lift force vector.
